content: Mutations in the KCNJ11 and ABCC8 genes can result in neonatal diabetes, which may be either transient or permanent depending on the specific mutation. Infants with these mutations may respond to treatment with oral sulfonylureas instead of requiring insulin therapy. Mutations in the INS gene are associated with permanent neonatal diabetes. This genetic alteration disrupts the production of insulin within the pancreatic beta cells, necessitating lifelong insulin therapy. Abnormalities involving the 6q24 region, specifically in the PLAGL1 and HYMAI genes, are linked to transient neonatal diabetes mellitus. This condition is often associated with uniparental disomy and may present with recurrent symptoms during adolescence. Mutations in the EIF2AK3 gene cause Wolcott-Rallison Syndrome, a recessive disorder characterized by permanent neonatal diabetes. This syndrome is also associated with additional clinical features, including skeletal abnormalities and liver dysfunction. FOXP3 gene mutations result in IPEX Syndrome, an X-linked immune disorder. This condition includes diabetes as a clinical feature, along with other autoimmune and inflammatory symptoms.
